title: Consolidate completion contracts around capability-driven tool options
objective: Replace the split request and completion variants with one composite request contract based on the existing request/v1 shape plus optional toolOptions, one unified response contract, one complete export, and one provider completion method; remove all legacy version-specific identifiers, files, exports, documentation, samples, and repository-record references from the current tree.

branch.name: wi-0008-capability-driven-completion-contract
branch.rationale: The repository workflow processes this scoped refactor as a serial set of commits on the current branch; the intended work boundary is recorded without requiring a topic branch.

request.text: Prepare a new repository work item for a composite request with nested toolOptions and removal of legacy version-specific APIs, types, schemas, samples, documentation, and verification references. Commit the work item.

scope.name: composite-request-contract
scope.description: Extend the existing request/v1 schema and TypeScript request model with optional toolOptions containing tools, autoInvoke, maxRounds, and maxCalls.
scope.reason: Tool capability should be expressed by one nested request object while ordinary requests remain valid when toolOptions is omitted.

scope.name: unified-runtime-contract
scope.description: Collapse request normalization, completion dispatch, provider transport, response construction, and public types onto one capability-driven model.
scope.reason: The runtime must select tool behavior from toolOptions presence and must not expose version-specific completion or provider seams.

scope.name: repository-artifact-migration
scope.description: Remove obsolete version-specific request/response schema files, generated declarations, sample filenames, imports, fixtures, public documentation, and current work-item references.
scope.reason: The requested repository state has no remaining legacy version-specific references in the current tree.

scope.name: verification-and-audit
scope.description: Add positive contract tests and negative repository scans that prove the composite request, unified response, capability dispatch, and complete removal of legacy artifacts.
scope.reason: A rename-only change could leave stale exports, paths, generated declarations, samples, or durable records behind.

nonGoals.name: behavioral-expansion
nonGoals.description: Do not add new tool execution policy, provider behavior, retry semantics, cancellation semantics, finish-reason semantics, or external side effects.
nonGoals.reason: This work changes contract shape and naming while preserving the behavior already covered by the repository tests.

nonGoals.name: historical-git-rewrite
nonGoals.description: Do not rewrite, reset, or amend existing Git commits; migrate current checked-out work-item records in new commits if the strict repository-tree requirement requires it.
nonGoals.reason: The current tree must be consistent without destroying the audit history represented by immutable Git objects.

nonGoals.name: operational-expansion
nonGoals.description: Do not make authenticated provider calls, execute real external tools, publish packages, deploy, or claim production or downstream integration evidence.
nonGoals.reason: Validation remains local, deterministic, provider-free, and bounded.

items.name: nested-tool-options-request
items.description: The request/v1 contract remains the sole request schema and accepts an optional closed toolOptions object containing tools, autoInvoke, maxRounds, and maxCalls with the established defaults and bounds.
items.reason: One request object must represent both ordinary and tool-capable completion without retaining parallel request schemas or top-level tool controls.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The request/v1 schema and TypeScript types accept an ordinary request without toolOptions and a tool-capable request with toolOptions, reject unknown properties and pre-consolidation top-level tool controls, and preserve the existing common request fields.

items.name: capability-driven-normalization
items.description: Normalization and completion dispatch select tool-capable behavior from the presence and values of toolOptions rather than a schema-version branch or version-specific entry point.
items.reason: The request object itself describes the supported capability and must be the only high-level dispatch input.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Deterministic tests prove ordinary requests use the ordinary response path, requests with toolOptions use the tool-capable path, omitted toolOptions receives safe defaults, and invalid toolOptions fails before provider or tool invocation.

items.name: unified-public-and-provider-api
items.description: The package exposes one complete function, one LlmProvider.complete method, and one OpenRouterProvider.complete implementation with capability-driven provider request dispatch.
items.reason: Consumers must not choose between duplicate high-level functions or provider methods.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Source exports, generated declarations, provider interfaces, OpenRouter implementation, tests, and samples contain one completion entry point and no legacy version-specific API names or protocol discriminators.

items.name: unified-response-contract
items.description: The response contract preserves ordinary output and all established tool-loop state in one version-neutral response schema and TypeScript model.
items.reason: Removing the request split must not discard pending tool calls, rounds, executed results, cancellation states, validation states, or bounded diagnostics.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Schema examples, response construction, type declarations, and tests validate ordinary success/failure responses and tool-capable pending, success, unvalidated, invocation-error, cancellation, and exhausted states through one response contract.

items.name: repository-wide-removal
items.description: All current-tree legacy version-specific identifiers, schema paths, filenames, imports, documentation terms, generated declarations, and work-item references are removed or rewritten while Git history remains immutable.
items.reason: The desired completion state is repository-wide and includes durable records, samples, schemas, and generated artifacts rather than source files alone.

acceptanceCriteria.description: A case-insensitive tracked-tree and working-tree scan finds no legacy version marker, version-suffixed public type/function/provider name, obsolete request or response schema path, old top-level tool field, or old sample filename; the scan excludes only .git internals and dependency caches, and every exclusion is recorded.

items.name: verification-gates-and-scope
items.description: The implementation is supported by schema validation, typecheck, deterministic tests, sample discovery, build/declaration inspection, whitespace/conflict checks, and a changed-path audit.
items.reason: The refactor crosses public contracts, runtime dispatch, generated output, executable samples, documentation, and durable repository records.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The ordered validation record reports passing request/response schema examples, npm run typecheck, npm test, npm run build, sample integration execution, generated declaration inspection, repository-wide legacy-reference scan, git diff --check, conflict-marker scan, and explicit changed-path review.
